directories.description: WHO SMART Trust's IG Publisher AST, INGESTED here although the IG's source is not (owner, 2026-10-04: an IG's semi-static KG may stay remote, and its AST is still ingested into the folio). Read from the branch family cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/ on the IG's own repository (litlfred/smart-trust; it could instead be materialised onto a local branch here, by dropping `repository`), one branch per IG package id; this IG's member is cat/fhir-harness/fhir-ast/smart.who.int.trust. Restored by fhir-harness/scripts/ig-cache.sh; absent from the checkout by design. Bean lehh.

The IG's artefact index. `index.json`, `menu.json`, `releases.json`, `package.tgz` and `sidecars/` are NOT COMMITTED: fhir-harness's `ig-index:build` writes them at publish from the IG's AST (`builtAtPublish`, fhir-harness#124; `sidecars/` via smart-base's `ig-site:sidecars` step, bean `4u5d`), replacing the reconstructed index and its committed `dak/` sidecars (retired in bean `4u5d`). `ig-identity.json` and `README.md` stay committed. `index.json` carries a `provenance` block naming the AST or config file every field came out of.
directories.readOnlyBasis: Built from the IG's own AST, and GENERATED -- fhir-harness's `ig-index:build` writes this index at publish, a person does not edit or commit it (fhir-harness#124). Read-only is about the second: a hand edit here silently changes what this repository claims upstream published, and `check:materialized-fixity` is what catches one that happened.

directories.description: How this IG realises the document kinds of the layers it needs: today `dak.coverage.smart-trust.json`, the DAK view of `fhir-artifact-index/`, which places each artefact in one of the ten DAK components by its FHIR resource type and lists what no rule places. GENERATED at publish by the DAK layer's `gen-document-kinds.ts` (`bun run cat smart-base:document-kinds`; declared `builtAtPublish`, because the index it reads is built at publish too, fhir-harness#124) into this directory, and not committed, because the report is about this IG: it lived beside the DAK kind in the layer below until wrong-direction move M13 (folio-assistant#2598), where it was a lower layer holding a file about a higher one. Declared with its file in one commit, per bean `dh4f`.

The OpenAPI documents this instance holds, ingested by the cat-openapi harness from the sources `cat-openapi.config.json` names (bean `s4ta`). Today one: the trust network gateway's API, which the IG's published `openapi/` carries as a vendored Swagger UI and which `ingest-ig-artifacts.ts` deliberately does not treat as the IG's own API. Each document is held VERBATIM beside a `<id>.source.json` recording the repository, path and commit it was read from; every operation in it is a node of this graph, with a page and an IRI here (`gateway/<operationId>/`, `gateway/<operationId>.jsonld`), written by `cat-openapi/scripts/gen-openapi-pages.ts`; the pages fetch the document beside them, and are complete HTML, so `served` publishes all of it verbatim.
directories.readOnlyBasis: Copies of an upstream API description (each a materialized node, `<id>.source.json`) and pages generated from it; `ingest-openapi.ts` and `gen-openapi-pages.ts` rewrite them, a person does not. A hand edit would silently change what this repository claims the API's authors published — the two scripts' `--check` is what catches one.

directories.description: The reader-facing pages, generated from `fhir-artifact-index/index.json` by `smart-trust:pages` (`fhir-harness/scripts/gen-ig-pages.ts`). SINCE 2026-10-05 THESE ARE THE ARTEFACT PAGES OF ONE SITE (`igSite`, bean `mftp`): they build into smart-trust's own IG site at `/smart-trust/` under the IG's menu, and the index, menu-section and category pages this description goes on to mention are no longer written -- the IG's own index, toc and artifacts pages replace them. What follows is the history of how the directory got here. THE REASON THIS EXISTS: `fhir-artifact-index` is registered `renderable: false`, and until 2026-09-21 this instance declared only that kind — so 674 ingested artefacts were reachable at no URL, which is how the owner found it, by asking where `/smart-trust` was. Only `docs` and `folio` are renderable, and `mount-instance-docs.ts` copies any declared `docs` directory as FINISHED HTML (Jekyll's source is hardcoded to `cat-harness/docs`, so an instance's own pages are built by nothing). `instanceRoot: true` is what makes THIS kind answer at `/smart-trust/` rather than the choice falling to sort order — the defect `withRoutes` documents. It is the only renderable kind here today, so nothing is ambiguous yet; declaring it now means adding a second one later cannot silently move the root. Generated, never authored: `smart-trust:pages:check` is the gate. The viewer for this instance's docs, BUILT BY cat-harness — the owner's rule that a harness which instantiates a directory makes a visualiser for it. Declared HERE, in this instance's own file, rather than in the root's: `compose-docs.docsLayers` treats every docs-kind entry in `cat-harness.json` as a COMPOSITION LAYER, so declaring this directory there would overlay this instance's `index.md` onto the site's own. Measured — `compose-docs.test.ts` failed exactly that way when tried. The ref resolves because `injectRails` measures against the BUILT instance's docs prefix (cat-harness's), not the declaring instance's, which is the same reason `who-iris-library`'s cat-harness-built ref resolves today. This directory is NOT mounted: `mount-instance-docs` skips a docs directory with no `index.html`, and this one has none. The viewer is real regardless — `auto-docs` indexes the 20 pages it holds and publishes that page. "No verbatim mount" and "no viewer" are different facts, and declaring this is what stops the second being inferred from the first.
directories._comment_igSite: Built INTO smart-trust's own IG site at /smart-trust/, not composed into the main site (bean mftp, owner 2026-10-05: one site, "clean break on old beahviour, no redirect needed"). Until then these pages were COMPOSED into the main Jekyll site at /smart-trust/ while the IG's 42 narrative pages were a second site at /smart-trust/ig/ built only in staging previews -- so production /smart-trust/ showed an artefact index and none of WHO's narrative pages. Now `stage-ig-sites.ts` copies this directory's artefact pages and assets into the IG's Jekyll source, under the IG's own menu, and `gen-ig-pages.ts` no longer writes the index/menu/category pages the IG's own index, toc and artifacts pages replace. Still rendered THROUGH just-the-docs, as the 2026-09-21 ruling asked ("i want the input/page(s)/ content to be rendered viajustthedocs pipeline"). who-iris does NOT set this and must not: it is a replica of IRIS.

directories.description: L1 source documents materialized for smart-trust: the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2 (9 October 2026), the legal source document for GDHCN definitions and Trust Domains (owner, 2026-11-01: "admin framework is the legal source document for GDHCN"). Every knowledge-graph reference to the Framework resolves through here, and `check:materialized-fixity` verifies its SHA-256 digest against `catalogue/`.

Qualified Dublin Core (`folio-dublin-core/v1`) and materialization fixity (`folio-catalogue-node/v1`) records for the documents materialized in `library/`: the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2. `bun run cat check:catalogue` and `bun run cat check:materialized-fixity` verify every node, metadataRef, libraryId, localPath and SHA-256 digest.
directories.readOnlyBasis: Records of a WHO document materialized in `library/`; `check:materialized-fixity` verifies the SHA-256 digests recorded here against `library/`.

directories.description: The primary GDHCN glossary (`gdhcn.glossary.json`, folio-glossary/v1): the 21 definitions in Section II of the GDHCN Administrative and Operational Framework 1.2, quoted from the L1 copy in `library/`. The Framework is the legal source (owner, 2026-11-01); IG-only terms may be added in a separate scheme and never override it. Rendered and checked by check:glossary.

smart-trust's bibliography: one folio-reference/v1 CSL-JSON entry per cited work, `<key>.json`, taken from the hand-written reference lists of the IG pages (certificate governance, references, ethical principles, decision support, TNG architecture). The pages' lists are written from these entries by `input/scripts/references.ts` between `references:begin`/`references:end` markers, and each in-text citation links to its entry's `#ref-<key>` anchor; `--check` fails on a stale list, a missing entry or a dangling citation.

The gettext side of smart-trust's own strings, one directory per target locale: today the `glossary/` templates of the GDHCN glossary (`glossary/gdhcn.glossary.json`). A scheme's translations sit with the instance whose terms they translate (owner, 2026-10-04, bean riit). Written by `bun run cat glossary:pot`.

_avatar_comment: A shield with a keyhole — a trust framework, about who may open what. NOT the shield-with-check: that is `qa`'s, and the registry refuses two kinds sharing a glyph. WHO BLUE, like smart-base: an organisation's published colour on a neutral glyph is not its identity, which is the line the owner drew for who-iris on 2026-09-23. Added 2026-10-04 (bean `2vpn`) when the owner chose a glyph over the shared operations card it had borrowed through a sticky. Moved here from cat-harness/schemas/avatars.ts, 2026-10-05 (bean sod4 #4): an instance declares its own mark.
_comment_site: The WHO SMART Trust implementation guide (FHIR IG source under input/), as a harnessed instance of smart-base. Its artefact index (fhir-artifact-index/), its OpenAPI graph (openapi/) and its generated IG-site pages (docs/, generated by smart-trust:pages and built at publish, never committed) are declared here, so its own site is built by the platform's one publish path (stage-local -> build-instance-site, site.build in smart-trust.config.json) as folio-site.yml built it.
_builtAtPublish_comment: Owner, 2026-10-14 (B1; schemas/built-at-publish.ts in cat-harness). This instance's JSON-LD @context is generated by `jsonld:contexts` (cat-harness-tools scripts/gen-instance-contexts.ts) from the prefixes and content-context terms its documents use, flattened with the prefix tables of every instance it needs. Those tables are read at the CHECKOUT's pins, not at pins this instance's commit names, so no commit of it can hold the file current: it is built at publish and never committed (bean folio-assistant-63q4). docs/ joined the list on 2026-10-15 (owner, ~10:45Z, B1): its pages are rendered by `smart-trust:pages` (fhir-harness gen-ig-pages over fhir-artifact-index/, with smart-base's themes and chrome), so they are a function of those layers at the checkout's pins: fhir-harness's switch to thin .html shells on 2026-10-14 made every committed page stale without a commit here. The index that mounts this instance registers `smart-trust:pages` at its root (a mounted instance cannot own a checkout script there), and derive:publish builds the directory; `directory` names the declared entry it fills, so check:declared-dirs and check:declaration-resolution do not expect it on disk before publish, and check:docs-populated does not grade pages a writer produced as authored documentation. The one committed file, docs/README.md, a three-line copy of the README's opening, went with it: nothing declared built at publish is tracked.
